Editor's letter

About this guide

An independent guide to established real estate developers active in Netanya, Israel. Discover their backgrounds, areas of activity, and official websites.

From new towers above the cliffs of Park HaYam to large-scale urban renewal in established neighbourhoods, Netanya is one of the most active residential markets on Israel's coast. This guide introduces some of the companies behind that change — in their own context, in plain language, and with a direct link to each developer's official website.

The Developers

Four established developers, selected editorially and presented in no particular order. Not a ranking.

Chapter I Editorial profile

Azorim

“Azorim is a Tel Aviv Stock Exchange-listed residential developer that has been building homes across Israel for around six decades.”

Azorim is one of Israel's longest-established residential developers, with a track record that stretches back to the mid-1960s. The company is publicly traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange and is chaired by its owner, Hershey Friedman. Its portfolio covers new-build neighbourhoods and towers in cities including Jerusalem, Tel Aviv, Haifa, Bat Yam and Be'er Sheva, alongside a dedicated urban renewal division and a rental arm.

Key areas of activity

  • New-build residential towers
  • Urban renewal
  • Rental housing (Azorim Living)
  • Coastal neighbourhoods in central Israel

Chapter II Editorial profile

Aura Israel

“Aura is a Tel Aviv Stock Exchange-listed developer that concentrates on urban renewal, replacing ageing housing blocks with new residential districts.”

Aura Israel, whose listed entity trades on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange as Aura Investments, was founded and is run by its controlling shareholder, lawyer Yaacov Atrakchi. The company presents itself primarily as an urban renewal specialist, working with owners of older buildings to demolish and rebuild them at higher density under pinui-binui and similar schemes, while also developing some new neighbourhoods.

Key areas of activity

  • Urban renewal (pinui-binui)
  • Large-scale residential redevelopment
  • New residential neighbourhoods
  • Mixed-use projects with commercial space

Chapter III Editorial profile

Africa Israel Residences

“Africa Israel Residences is the TASE-listed homebuilding arm of the Africa Israel group, known for its Savyonim-branded residential communities.”

Africa Israel Residences develops and builds housing across Israel and is controlled by Africa Israel Investments. Its shares trade on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Much of its output is marketed under the Savyonim name, a brand that traces back to the company's first neighbourhood in the town of Savyon and is applied to planned communities that include green space and local services alongside the apartments. An urban renewal subsidiary, Africa Urban Renewal, handles redevelopment schemes.

Key areas of activity

  • Savyonim-branded residential communities
  • Urban renewal (Africa Urban Renewal)
  • High-rise coastal housing
  • Projects across central Israel, Jerusalem and the north

Chapter IV Editorial profile

Ashtrom Residences

“Ashtrom Residences, formerly Ashdar, is the wholly owned residential development arm of the TASE-listed Ashtrom Group.”

Ashtrom Residences is the homebuilding subsidiary of Ashtrom Group, one of Israel's largest construction and real estate groups, whose shares trade on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. The company operated for decades as Ashdar before being rebranded under the parent group's name, and it reports more than 40 years of experience planning and building residential projects. It is led by CEO Arnon Friedman.

Key areas of activity

  • New-build residential projects
  • Urban renewal (pinui-binui and NOP 38)
  • Combination transactions with landowners
  • Central Israel and major cities nationwide
